title: 2001 HMMT February Team Problem 4
statement: P is a polynomial. When P is divided by \(x-1\), the remainder is -4 . When P is divided by \(x-2\), the remainder is -1 . When \(P\) is divided by \(x-3\), the remainder is 4 . Determine the remainder when P is divided by \(x^{3}-6 x^{2}+11 x-6\).

solutions.text: The remainder polynomial is simply the order two polynomial that goes through the points \((1,-4),(2,-1)\), and \((3,4): x^{2}-5\).
